title: I2S TDM and PDM overview: establish format and clock ownership
summary: Specify which device drives each clock, the sample rate, framing, slot width and active data directions. PDM reception requires compatible hardware or conversion to PCM.
applies_to: Digital audio links; the cited converter illustrates supported formats.
required_inputs: Endpoint formats, clock roles and I/O voltages
verification: Check both endpoints agree on framing and sample timing.
limitations: Do not assume identical pin labels imply compatible framing or that every I2S receiver accepts PDM.

title: I2S and TDM clock and data routing pattern
summary: Route bit clock, frame synchronization and each data direction according to the selected endpoint connection; separate sensitive circuitry from noisy power paths.
applies_to: Board-level audio; TAS2563 connections illustrate one implementation.
required_inputs: Clock ownership, data directions, slot mapping and endpoint timing
verification: Verify framing and audio transfer with every intended channel enabled.
limitations: Device-specific unused-pin and stereo-chain instructions are not general I2S rules.

citations.locator: Typical application schematics; Layout Guidelines Summary, pages 27-29

pattern.diagram: Clock owner BCLK/FSYNC -> Receivers; transmitter SDOUT -> receiver SDIN
placement: Place connected audio devices to limit channel length.
routing: Review clock loading and data timing; MCLK is device-dependent.
pitfalls: Do not tie multiple active clock outputs together.

title: PDM microphone clock and data pattern
summary: Supply the microphone clock and connect PDM data to a compatible receiver. Match channel edge selection and decimation configuration to the microphone.
applies_to: Digital PDM microphones and compatible receivers or converters.
required_inputs: Microphone clock, voltage, edge and receiver requirements
verification: Verify clock, channel assignment and recovered audio.
limitations: Shared data wiring requires compatible output-enable timing; do not parallel arbitrary microphone outputs.

citations.locator: Sections 7.3 and 8.2, digital microphone configuration and typical application

pattern.diagram: Receiver PDMCLK -> Microphone; microphone DATA -> PDM input
placement: Place bypass capacitors at the microphone supply.
return_path: Keep clock and data referenced to ground.
pitfalls: PDM is not PCM framing; conversion may be required.
